Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to be hashed. May be empty.
Output: String - a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, or
        an empty string when verification is disabled.
Pre-condition: data is not null. The verification configuration has been
               initialized via initializeIngredients().
Post-condition: The returned string is either empty (none mode) or a
                64-character lowercase hex digest that is deterministic
                for a given data payload.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData
Summary: Reverses the compression step applied by processData,
         returning the original byte stream.
Algorithm:
  1. If compression equals CompressionMethod::none, return data unchanged.
  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     decompression on data and return the decompressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - bytes that were produced by processData.
Output: EByteArray - the original bytes before compression.
Pre-condition: data is not null. compression setting matches the one
               used when data was produced.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) equals x for any x under
                a stable compression configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary: Recovers the original byte array from an EMap representation
         of a binary wrapper (the structure produced by PreparedData
         toMap()), preserving the MIME type.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. content = data.get("content") as String (Base64).
  3. mime    = data.get("mime_type") as String (may be null).
  4. size    = data.get("size") as int (informational).
  5. bytes   = Base64.decode(content).
  6. Return a two-element list [bytes, mime] as List<EJavaObject>.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input: data (EMap) - map containing keys "content" (Base64 String),
       "mime_type" (String, optional), and "size" (int, informational).
Output: List<EJavaObject> - two-element list [EByteArray bytes,
        String mimeType]. mimeType may be null.
Pre-condition: data is not null and contains at least a "content" entry
               whose value is a valid Base64 String.
Post-condition: The returned bytes, MIME type, and (when verified) size
                match the values originally used to build the wrapper.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary: Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text it
         represents, reversing the text encoding pipeline (unprocess,
         uncompress, UTF-8 decode).
Algorithm:
  1. If emojiData is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. If emojiData is empty, return an empty string (round-trip case).
  3. Map each emoji symbol back to its chunk value via reverseMap;
     reject any symbol not present in reverseMap by throwing
     IllegalArgumentException.
  4. Concatenate the chunk bits into a single bit stream.
  5. Call unprocessData(bitStream) to reverse the optional compression
     step.
  6. Convert the resulting byte array to a UTF-8 String and return it.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, reverseMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: emojiData (String) - a non-null sequence of emoji symbols, each
       belonging to the currently configured alphabet. May be empty.
Output: String - the decoded UTF-8 text. Empty when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
               reverseMap are populated. compression is one of the values
               defined in CompressionMethod.
Post-condition: For non-empty input, all symbols are recognized; output is
                valid UTF-8 and is the exact original text that would be
                produced by encode() on the same recipe/compression
                configuration.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into an emoji string using the
         current recipe, optional compression, and the configured
         emoji alphabet.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. Convert data to a UTF-8 byte array.
  3. Call processData(bytes) to apply optional compression.
  4. Convert the processed byte stream into a bit stream.
  5. Split the bit stream into chunks of bitsPerChunk bits each
     (zero-pad the final chunk if shorter).
  6. For each chunk, compute its integer value and look up the
     corresponding emoji symbol in emojiMap (values >= baseSize are
     impossible by construction of the chunk size).
  7. Concatenate the symbols and return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod, mask
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (String) - the text to encode as UTF-8. May be empty.
Output: String - an emoji sequence representing the encoded data. Empty
        string when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
               the recipe parameters are ready. The compression setting
               is one of the CompressionMethod constants.
Post-condition: decode(encode(data)) returns the original text for any
                non-null UTF-8 string under the same configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData
Summary: Inverse of prepareBinaryData. Decodes Base64 content and
         returns the original byte array, preserving the MIME type
         and recorded size.
Algorithm:
  1. If preparedData is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. bytes = Base64.decode(preparedData.content).
  3. If preparedData.size >= 0, truncate or trust bytes according to
     recorded size (implementation detail: rely on size for reporting;
     bytes are returned in their decoded form).
  4. Return bytes.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input: preparedData (PreparedData) - wrapper produced by
       prepareBinaryData(); not null.
Output: EByteArray - decoded raw bytes. May be empty.
Pre-condition: preparedData.content is valid Base64. The wrapper was
               produced by prepareBinaryData() or otherwise conforms to
               its field semantics.
Post-condition: Returned byte array's length equals preparedData.size
                and its Base64 encoding equals preparedData.content.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary: Wraps a binary payload and MIME type into a JSON-compatible
         text structure, then emoji-encodes the wrapper, returning a
         single emoji string that round-trips back to the original
         bytes via decodeBinary().
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke prepareBinaryData(mimeType, data) to build a PreparedData
     object with Base64-encoded content, the MIME type, and the byte
     size.
  2. Convert the PreparedData to its EMap representation via toMap().
  3. Serialize the map to a JSON-like string.
  4. Call encode(serialized) to produce the final emoji string and
     return it.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod, emojiMap, recipeType
Related Classes: CompressionMethod, PreparedData
Input:
  mimeType (String) - MIME type to record; may be null when unknown.
  data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to encode; may be empty but not null.
Output: String - an emoji sequence that represents the serialized binary
        wrapper. Empty when data is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been called. data is not
               null. MIME type, when provided, follows standard
               type/subtype format.
Post-condition: decodeBinary(encodeBinary(mimeType, data)) returns a
                list whose first element equals data and whose MIME
                type matches the supplied mimeType (or is null).

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary: Inspects a file path and returns its size, MIME type,
         processability flag, and a suggested recipe, packaged in an
         EMap. When the file cannot be processed, the returned map
         contains an "error" entry and "can_process" set to false.
Algorithm:
  1. Attempt to read the file via FileHandler::readFile.
     - If reading fails, return a map { "error": message,
       "can_process": false }.
  2. Determine MIME type using FileHandler::guessMimeType with a
     fallback of "application/octet-stream".
  3. Compute suggested = suggestRecipe(content.length).
  4. Build and return a map containing:
       size        -> long, byte size of the file
       mime_type   -> String, detected or fallback MIME
       can_process -> true
       suggested_recipe -> String, one of quick/light/classic/gourmet
Related Features: recipeType
Related Classes: FileHandler
Input: filePath (String) - absolute or relative path to an existing file.
Output: String (EMap serialized) - map of file metadata with keys
        size, mime_type, can_process, suggested_recipe, or, on error,
        error and can_process=false.
Pre-condition: filePath is a syntactically valid path string. No file
               existence guarantee; missing or unreadable files produce
               an error entry.
Post-condition: For a readable file the map describes the actual file
                and a suggested recipe that scales with its size. For
                an unreadable file the map explicitly reports the error
                and indicates can_process=false.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary: Picks a recipe name based on the size of the payload in bytes,
         following the documented thresholds.
Algorithm:
  1. If size < 1024 (1 KB), return "quick".
  2. Else if size < 10240 (10 KB), return "light".
  3. Else if size < 102400 (100 KB), return "classic".
  4. Else return "gourmet".
Related Features: recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input: size (int) - payload length in bytes; non-negative.
Output: String - one of "quick", "light", "classic", "gourmet".
Pre-condition: size >= 0.
Post-condition: Returned value is always a supported recipe and matches
    the file-size bucket the input falls into.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary: Applies the configured compression (if any) to a byte array,
         preparing it for bit-level chunking during encoding.
Algorithm:
  1. If compression equals CompressionMethod::none, return data unchanged.
  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     compression on data and return the compressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged (defensive
     default) or throw an IllegalStateException for invalid configuration.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - raw bytes to compress; may be empty.
Output: EByteArray - bytes after optional compression. Equal to the input
        when compression is "none".
Pre-condition: data is not null. compression is a known
               CompressionMethod constant.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) reconstructs x for any
                input x (round-trip property).

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary: Builds a PreparedData wrapper describing a binary payload by
         Base64-encoding its bytes and recording the MIME type and
         byte size.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. content = Base64.encode(data).
  3. size = data.length.
  4. Construct a new PreparedData(content, mimeType, size) and return it.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
  mimeType (String) - MIME type to associate with the payload; may be null.
  data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to wrap; may be empty but not null.
Output: PreparedData - object exposing content (Base64), mimeType, and
        size fields, and a toMap() returning {"content","mime_type","size"}.
Pre-condition: data is not null.
Post-condition: The returned PreparedData's content is valid Base64
                representing data exactly; size equals data.length;
                mimeType is preserved as supplied (may be null).

EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary: Computes encoding statistics comparing an original text string
         and its emoji-encoded counterpart.
Algorithm:
  1. Compute original_bytes = UTF-8 byte length of `original`.
  2. Compute encoded_length = character count of `encoded` (each emoji
     symbol counts as one).
  3. bits_per_emoji = bitsPerChunk.
  4. theoretical_ratio = encoded_length * bits_per_emoji / original_bytes
     (or 0 when original_bytes is 0, to avoid division by zero).
  5. actual_ratio = original_bytes / encoded_length (or 0 when
     encoded_length is 0).
  6. Build an EMap with entries: original_bytes, encoded_length,
     actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji. Return it as a
     String representation.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input:
  original (String) - the source UTF-8 text, may be empty.
  encoded  (String) - the emoji-encoded text, may be empty.
Output: String (EMap serialized) - map with keys original_bytes,
        encoded_length, actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji.
Pre-condition: Both arguments are non-null. `encoded` is assumed to be
               the result of encode(original) under the current recipe.
Post-condition: The returned map is internally consistent:
                theoretical_ratio uses bitsPerChunk derived from the recipe,
                and ratios are zero when the relevant divisor is zero.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary: Performs a file-oriented encode or decode operation,
         converting between raw bytes and an emoji string written to
         disk. Returns an EMap summarizing the result.
Algorithm:
  1. Read the input file using FileHandler::readFile(inputPath).
  2. If operation == "encode":
       a. mimeType = file.mimeType (or FileHandler::guessMimeType).
       b. emoji = encodeBinary(mimeType, file.content).
       c. result = { original_bytes: file.content.length,
                     encoded_length: emoji.length(),
                     mime_type: mimeType,
                     actual_ratio: file.content.length / emoji.length()
                      (0 when emoji is empty) }.
       d. Write emoji bytes to outputPath via FileHandler::writeFile.
  3. Else if operation == "decode":
       a. Read outputPath's bytes as a String emoji.
       b. list = decodeBinary(emoji).
       c. mime = list[1] (String).
       d. bytes = list[0] (EByteArray).
       e. Write bytes to inputPath via FileHandler::writeFile.
       f. result = { decoded_size: bytes.length, mime_type: mime }.
  4. Otherwise, return { error: "unknown operation", can_process: false }.
  5. Return result as a serialized EMap (String).
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod, emojiMap, reverseMap,
                  recipeType
Related Classes: CompressionMethod, FileData, FileHandler
Input:
  inputPath  (String) - path to the source file.
  outputPath (String) - path to the destination file.
  operation  (String) - either "encode" or "decode" (case-sensitive).
Output: String (EMap serialized) - file processing summary with keys
        original_bytes, encoded_length, mime_type, actual_ratio (encode)
        or decoded_size, mime_type (decode), or an error entry when the
        operation name is not recognized.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has run. For decode, outputPath
               contains an emoji string produced by this codec. The
               process has permission to read the input and write to
               the output.
Post-condition: After encode, outputPath holds an emoji string and the
               result map reports original_bytes and encoded_length.
               After decode, inputPath holds the recovered bytes and
               the result map reports decoded_size and mime_type.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary: Decodes an emoji string that wraps a serialized binary payload
         (Base64-encoded content plus MIME metadata) into the original
         byte array and MIME type.
Algorithm:
  1. Call decode(encoded) to obtain the JSON-like wrapper string.
  2. Parse the wrapper into an EMap with keys "content", "mime_type",
     and "size" (any other keys are ignored).
  3. Invoke restoreBinaryDataFromMap(map) to obtain the original
     EByteArray and MIME type.
  4. Return a List<EJavaObject> of size 2 whose first element is the
     restored byte array and whose second element is the MIME type
     string.
Related Features: reverseMap, emojiMap, compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: encoded (String) - a non-null emoji string produced by
       encodeBinary(). May be empty only when the original payload was
       empty.
Output: List<EJavaObject> - a two-element list [EByteArray content,
        String mimeType]. content is the original byte sequence; the
        MIME type string may be null when none was provided.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has run. The input string contains
               only emoji symbols from the active alphabet (or is empty).
Post-condition: The returned byte array matches the bytes originally
                passed to encodeBinary() and the MIME type matches the
                value supplied at encoding time. The size stored in the
                wrapper equals content.length.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary: Computes a verification hash over a byte array according to the
         active verification method (currently sha256 or none). Returns a
         lowercase hexadecimal digest, zero-padded when necessary, or an
         empty string when verification is disabled.
Algorithm:
  1. If verificationMethod equals VerificationMethod::none,
     return an empty string.
  2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
  3. Format the resulting 32 raw bytes as a 64-character lowercase
     hexadecimal string (zero-padded with leading zeros for any byte
     whose high nibble is 0).
  4. Return the formatted digest.
Related Features: verification, verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to be hashed. May be empty.
Output: String - a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, or
        an empty string when verification is disabled.
Pre-condition: data is not null. The verification configuration has been
               initialized via initializeIngredients().
Post-condition: The returned string is either empty (none mode) or a
                64-character lowercase hex digest that is deterministic
                for a given data payload.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData

  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     decompression on data and return the decompressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - bytes that were produced by processData.
Output: EByteArray - the original bytes before compression.

               used when data was produced.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) equals x for any x under
                a stable compression configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap

  3. mime    = data.get("mime_type") as String (may be null).
  4. size    = data.get("size") as int (informational).
  5. bytes   = Base64.decode(content).
  6. Return a two-element list [bytes, mime] as List<EJavaObject>.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input: data (EMap) - map containing keys "content" (Base64 String),
       "mime_type" (String, optional), and "size" (int, informational).

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary: Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text it
         represents, reversing the text encoding pipeline (unprocess,
         uncompress, UTF-8 decode).
Algorithm:

  2. If emojiData is empty, return an empty string (round-trip case).
  3. Map each emoji symbol back to its chunk value via reverseMap;

  4. Concatenate the chunk bits into a single bit stream.
  5. Call unprocessData(bitStream) to reverse the optional compression
     step.
  6. Convert the resulting byte array to a UTF-8 String and return it.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, reverseMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: emojiData (String) - a non-null sequence of emoji symbols, each
       belonging to the currently configured alphabet. May be empty.
Output: String - the decoded UTF-8 text. Empty when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and

Post-condition: For non-empty input, all symbols are recognized; output is
                valid UTF-8 and is the exact original text that would be
                produced by encode() on the same recipe/compression
                configuration.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into an emoji string using the
         current recipe, optional compression, and the configured
         emoji alphabet.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. Convert data to a UTF-8 byte array.
  3. Call processData(bytes) to apply optional compression.
  4. Convert the processed byte stream into a bit stream.
  5. Split the bit stream into chunks of bitsPerChunk bits each
     (zero-pad the final chunk if shorter).
  6. For each chunk, compute its integer value and look up the
     corresponding emoji symbol in emojiMap (values >= baseSize are
     impossible by construction of the chunk size).
  7. Concatenate the symbols and return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod, mask
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (String) - the text to encode as UTF-8. May be empty.
Output: String - an emoji sequence representing the encoded data. Empty
        string when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
               the recipe parameters are ready. The compression setting
               is one of the CompressionMethod constants.
Post-condition: decode(encode(data)) returns the original text for any
                non-null UTF-8 string under the same configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData
Summary: Inverse of prepareBinaryData. Decodes Base64 content and
         returns the original byte array, preserving the MIME type
         and recorded size.
Algorithm:
  1. If preparedData is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. bytes = Base64.decode(preparedData.content).
  3. If preparedData.size >= 0, truncate or trust bytes according to
     recorded size (implementation detail: rely on size for reporting;
     bytes are returned in their decoded form).
  4. Return bytes.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input: preparedData (PreparedData) - wrapper produced by
       prepareBinaryData(); not null.
Output: EByteArray - decoded raw bytes. May be empty.
Pre-condition: preparedData.content is valid Base64. The wrapper was
               produced by prepareBinaryData() or otherwise conforms to
               its field semantics.
Post-condition: Returned byte array's length equals preparedData.size
                and its Base64 encoding equals preparedData.content.

EmojiCodec::encodeBinary
Summary: Wraps a binary payload and MIME type into a JSON-compatible
         text structure, then emoji-encodes the wrapper, returning a
         single emoji string that round-trips back to the original
         bytes via decodeBinary().
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke prepareBinaryData(mimeType, data) to build a PreparedData
     object with Base64-encoded content, the MIME type, and the byte
     size.
  2. Convert the PreparedData to its EMap representation via toMap().
  3. Serialize the map to a JSON-like string.
  4. Call encode(serialized) to produce the final emoji string and
     return it.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod, emojiMap, recipeType
Related Classes: CompressionMethod, PreparedData
Input:
  mimeType (String) - MIME type to record; may be null when unknown.
  data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to encode; may be empty but not null.
Output: String - an emoji sequence that represents the serialized binary
        wrapper. Empty when data is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been called. data is not
               null. MIME type, when provided, follows standard
               type/subtype format.
Post-condition: decodeBinary(encodeBinary(mimeType, data)) returns a
                list whose first element equals data and whose MIME
                type matches the supplied mimeType (or is null).

EmojiCodec::getFileInfo
Summary: Inspects a file path and returns its size, MIME type,
         processability flag, and a suggested recipe, packaged in an
         EMap. When the file cannot be processed, the returned map
         contains an "error" entry and "can_process" set to false.
Algorithm:
  1. Attempt to read the file via FileHandler::readFile.
     - If reading fails, return a map { "error": message,
       "can_process": false }.
  2. Determine MIME type using FileHandler::guessMimeType with a
     fallback of "application/octet-stream".
  3. Compute suggested = suggestRecipe(content.length).
  4. Build and return a map containing:
       size        -> long, byte size of the file
       mime_type   -> String, detected or fallback MIME
       can_process -> true
       suggested_recipe -> String, one of quick/light/classic/gourmet
Related Features: recipeType
Related Classes: FileHandler
Input: filePath (String) - absolute or relative path to an existing file.
Output: String (EMap serialized) - map of file metadata with keys
        size, mime_type, can_process, suggested_recipe, or, on error,
        error and can_process=false.
Pre-condition: filePath is a syntactically valid path string. No file
               existence guarantee; missing or unreadable files produce
               an error entry.
Post-condition: For a readable file the map describes the actual file
                and a suggested recipe that scales with its size. For
                an unreadable file the map explicitly reports the error
                and indicates can_process=false.

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary: Picks a recipe name based on the size of the payload in bytes,
         following the documented thresholds.
Algorithm:
  1. If size < 1024 (1 KB), return "quick".
  2. Else if size < 10240 (10 KB), return "light".
  3. Else if size < 102400 (100 KB), return "classic".
  4. Else return "gourmet".
Related Features: recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input: size (int) - payload length in bytes; non-negative.
Output: String - one of "quick", "light", "classic", "gourmet".
Pre-condition: size >= 0.
Post-condition: Returned value is always a supported recipe and matches
    the file-size bucket the input falls into.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary: Applies the configured compression (if any) to a byte array,
         preparing it for bit-level chunking during encoding.
Algorithm:
  1. If compression equals CompressionMethod::none, return data unchanged.
  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     compression on data and return the compressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged (defensive
     default) or throw an IllegalStateException for invalid configuration.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - raw bytes to compress; may be empty.
Output: EByteArray - bytes after optional compression. Equal to the input
        when compression is "none".
Pre-condition: data is not null. compression is a known
               CompressionMethod constant.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) reconstructs x for any
                input x (round-trip property).

EmojiCodec::prepareBinaryData
Summary: Builds a PreparedData wrapper describing a binary payload by
         Base64-encoding its bytes and recording the MIME type and
         byte size.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. content = Base64.encode(data).
  3. size = data.length.
  4. Construct a new PreparedData(content, mimeType, size) and return it.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input:
  mimeType (String) - MIME type to associate with the payload; may be null.
  data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to wrap; may be empty but not null.
Output: PreparedData - object exposing content (Base64), mimeType, and
        size fields, and a toMap() returning {"content","mime_type","size"}.
Pre-condition: data is not null.
Post-condition: The returned PreparedData's content is valid Base64
                representing data exactly; size equals data.length;
                mimeType is preserved as supplied (may be null).

EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary: Computes encoding statistics comparing an original text string
         and its emoji-encoded counterpart.
Algorithm:
  1. Compute original_bytes = UTF-8 byte length of `original`.
  2. Compute encoded_length = character count of `encoded` (each emoji
     symbol counts as one).
  3. bits_per_emoji = bitsPerChunk.
  4. theoretical_ratio = encoded_length * bits_per_emoji / original_bytes
     (or 0 when original_bytes is 0, to avoid division by zero).
  5. actual_ratio = original_bytes / encoded_length (or 0 when
     encoded_length is 0).
  6. Build an EMap with entries: original_bytes, encoded_length,
     actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji. Return it as a
     String representation.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input:
  original (String) - the source UTF-8 text, may be empty.
  encoded  (String) - the emoji-encoded text, may be empty.
Output: String (EMap serialized) - map with keys original_bytes,
        encoded_length, actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji.
Pre-condition: Both arguments are non-null. `encoded` is assumed to be
               the result of encode(original) under the current recipe.
Post-condition: The returned map is internally consistent:
                theoretical_ratio uses bitsPerChunk derived from the recipe,
                and ratios are zero when the relevant divisor is zero.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary: Performs a file-oriented encode or decode operation,
         converting between raw bytes and an emoji string written to
         disk. Returns an EMap summarizing the result.
Algorithm:
  1. Read the input file using FileHandler::readFile(inputPath).
  2. If operation == "encode":
       a. mimeType = file.mimeType (or FileHandler::guessMimeType).
       b. emoji = encodeBinary(mimeType, file.content).
       c. result = { original_bytes: file.content.length,
                     encoded_length: emoji.length(),
                     mime_type: mimeType,
                     actual_ratio: file.content.length / emoji.length()
                      (0 when emoji is empty) }.
       d. Write emoji bytes to outputPath via FileHandler::writeFile.
  3. Else if operation == "decode":
       a. Read outputPath's bytes as a String emoji.
       b. list = decodeBinary(emoji).
       c. mime = list[1] (String).
       d. bytes = list[0] (EByteArray).
       e. Write bytes to inputPath via FileHandler::writeFile.
       f. result = { decoded_size: bytes.length, mime_type: mime }.
  4. Otherwise, return { error: "unknown operation", can_process: false }.
  5. Return result as a serialized EMap (String).
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod, emojiMap, reverseMap,
                  recipeType
Related Classes: CompressionMethod, FileData, FileHandler
Input:
  inputPath  (String) - path to the source file.
  outputPath (String) - path to the destination file.
  operation  (String) - either "encode" or "decode" (case-sensitive).
Output: String (EMap serialized) - file processing summary with keys
        original_bytes, encoded_length, mime_type, actual_ratio (encode)
        or decoded_size, mime_type (decode), or an error entry when the
        operation name is not recognized.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has run. For decode, outputPath
               contains an emoji string produced by this codec. The
               process has permission to read the input and write to
               the output.
Post-condition: After encode, outputPath holds an emoji string and the
               result map reports original_bytes and encoded_length.
               After decode, inputPath holds the recovered bytes and
               the result map reports decoded_size and mime_type.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Operation Specifications
EmojiCodec::decodeBinary
Summary: Decodes an emoji string that wraps a serialized binary payload
         (Base64-encoded content plus MIME metadata) into the original
         byte array and MIME type.
Algorithm:
  1. Call decode(encoded) to obtain the JSON-like wrapper string.
  2. Parse the wrapper into an EMap with keys "content", "mime_type",
     and "size" (any other keys are ignored).
  3. Invoke restoreBinaryDataFromMap(map) to obtain the original
     EByteArray and MIME type.
  4. Return a List<EJavaObject> of size 2 whose first element is the
     restored byte array and whose second element is the MIME type
     string.
Related Features: reverseMap, emojiMap, compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: encoded (String) - a non-null emoji string produced by
       encodeBinary(). May be empty only when the original payload was
       empty.
Output: List<EJavaObject> - a two-element list [EByteArray content,
        String mimeType]. content is the original byte sequence; the
        MIME type string may be null when none was provided.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has run. The input string contains
               only emoji symbols from the active alphabet (or is empty).
Post-condition: The returned byte array matches the bytes originally
                passed to encodeBinary() and the MIME type matches the
                value supplied at encoding time. The size stored in the
                wrapper equals content.length.

EmojiCodec::calculateHash
Summary: Computes a verification hash over a byte array according to the
         active verification method (currently sha256 or none). Returns a
         lowercase hexadecimal digest, zero-padded when necessary, or an
         empty string when verification is disabled.
Algorithm:
  1. If verificationMethod equals VerificationMethod::none,
     return an empty string.
  2. Otherwise, compute SHA-256 over the input byte array.
  3. Format the resulting 32 raw bytes as a 64-character lowercase
     hexadecimal string (zero-padded with leading zeros for any byte
     whose high nibble is 0).
  4. Return the formatted digest.
Related Features: verification, verificationMethod
Related Classes: VerificationMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - the raw bytes to be hashed. May be empty.
Output: String - a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, or
        an empty string when verification is disabled.
Pre-condition: data is not null. The verification configuration has been
               initialized via initializeIngredients().
Post-condition: The returned string is either empty (none mode) or a
                64-character lowercase hex digest that is deterministic
                for a given data payload.

EmojiCodec::unprocessData
Summary: Reverses the compression step applied by processData,
         returning the original byte stream.
Algorithm:
  1. If compression equals CompressionMethod::none, return data unchanged.
  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     decompression on data and return the decompressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (EByteArray) - bytes that were produced by processData.
Output: EByteArray - the original bytes before compression.
Pre-condition: data is not null. compression setting matches the one
               used when data was produced.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) equals x for any x under
                a stable compression configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryDataFromMap
Summary: Recovers the original byte array from an EMap representation
         of a binary wrapper (the structure produced by PreparedData
         toMap()), preserving the MIME type.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. content = data.get("content") as String (Base64).
  3. mime    = data.get("mime_type") as String (may be null).
  4. size    = data.get("size") as int (informational).
  5. bytes   = Base64.decode(content).
  6. Return a two-element list [bytes, mime] as List<EJavaObject>.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: PreparedData
Input: data (EMap) - map containing keys "content" (Base64 String),
       "mime_type" (String, optional), and "size" (int, informational).
Output: List<EJavaObject> - two-element list [EByteArray bytes,
        String mimeType]. mimeType may be null.
Pre-condition: data is not null and contains at least a "content" entry
               whose value is a valid Base64 String.
Post-condition: The returned bytes, MIME type, and (when verified) size
                match the values originally used to build the wrapper.

EmojiCodec::decode
Summary: Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text it
         represents, reversing the text encoding pipeline (unprocess,
         uncompress, UTF-8 decode).
Algorithm:
  1. If emojiData is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. If emojiData is empty, return an empty string (round-trip case).
  3. Map each emoji symbol back to its chunk value via reverseMap;
     reject any symbol not present in reverseMap by throwing
     IllegalArgumentException.
  4. Concatenate the chunk bits into a single bit stream.
  5. Call unprocessData(bitStream) to reverse the optional compression
     step.
  6. Convert the resulting byte array to a UTF-8 String and return it.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, reverseMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: emojiData (String) - a non-null sequence of emoji symbols, each
       belonging to the currently configured alphabet. May be empty.
Output: String - the decoded UTF-8 text. Empty when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
               reverseMap are populated. compression is one of the values
               defined in CompressionMethod.
Post-condition: For non-empty input, all symbols are recognized; output is
                valid UTF-8 and is the exact original text that would be
                produced by encode() on the same recipe/compression
                configuration.

EmojiCodec::encode
Summary: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into an emoji string using the
         current recipe, optional compression, and the configured
         emoji alphabet.
Algorithm:
  1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
  2. Convert data to a UTF-8 byte array.
  3. Call processData(bytes) to apply optional compression.
  4. Convert the processed byte stream into a bit stream.
  5. Split the bit stream into chunks of bitsPerChunk bits each
     (zero-pad the final chunk if shorter).
  6. For each chunk, compute its integer value and look up the
     corresponding emoji symbol in emojiMap (values >= baseSize are
     impossible by construction of the chunk size).
  7. Concatenate the symbols and return the resulting emoji string.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, recipeType,
                  compression, compressionMethod, mask
Related Classes: CompressionMethod
Input: data (String) - the text to encode as UTF-8. May be empty.
Output: String - an emoji sequence representing the encoded data. Empty
        string when input is empty.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
               the recipe parameters are ready. The compression setting
               is one of the CompressionMethod constants.
Post-condition: decode(encode(data)) returns the original text for any
                non-null UTF-8 string under the same configuration.

EmojiCodec::restoreBinaryData

EmojiCodec::suggestRecipe
Summary: Picks a recipe name based on the size of the payload in bytes,

  2. Else if size < 10240 (10 KB), return "light".
  3. Else if size < 102400 (100 KB), return "classic".
  4. Else return "gourmet".
Related Features: recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input: size (int) - payload length in bytes; non-negative.
Output: String - one of "quick", "light", "classic", "gourmet".
Pre-condition: size >= 0.
Post-condition: Returned value is always a supported recipe and matches
    the file-size bucket the input falls into.

EmojiCodec::processData
Summary: Applies the configured compression (if any) to a byte array,
         preparing it for bit-level chunking during encoding.
Algorithm:
  1. If compression equals CompressionMethod::none, return data unchanged.
  2. If compression equals CompressionMethod::zlib, perform zlib
     compression on data and return the compressed bytes.
  3. For any other value, fall back to returning data unchanged (defensive
     default) or throw an IllegalStateException for invalid configuration.
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod
Related Classes: CompressionMethod

        when compression is "none".

               CompressionMethod constant.
Post-condition: unprocessData(processData(x)) reconstructs x for any
                input x (round-trip property).

         byte size.

Related Features: None

EmojiCodec::getStats
Summary: Computes encoding statistics comparing an original text string
         and its emoji-encoded counterpart.
Algorithm:
  1. Compute original_bytes = UTF-8 byte length of `original`.
  2. Compute encoded_length = character count of `encoded` (each emoji
     symbol counts as one).
  3. bits_per_emoji = bitsPerChunk.
  4. theoretical_ratio = encoded_length * bits_per_emoji / original_bytes
     (or 0 when original_bytes is 0, to avoid division by zero).
  5. actual_ratio = original_bytes / encoded_length (or 0 when
     encoded_length is 0).
  6. Build an EMap with entries: original_bytes, encoded_length,
     actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji. Return it as a
     String representation.
Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, recipeType
Related Classes: None
Input:
  original (String) - the source UTF-8 text, may be empty.
  encoded  (String) - the emoji-encoded text, may be empty.
Output: String (EMap serialized) - map with keys original_bytes,
        encoded_length, actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji.
Pre-condition: Both arguments are non-null. `encoded` is assumed to be
               the result of encode(original) under the current recipe.
Post-condition: The returned map is internally consistent:
                theoretical_ratio uses bitsPerChunk derived from the recipe,
                and ratios are zero when the relevant divisor is zero.

EmojiCodec::processFile
Summary: Performs a file-oriented encode or decode operation,
         converting between raw bytes and an emoji string written to
         disk. Returns an EMap summarizing the result.
Algorithm:
  1. Read the input file using FileHandler::readFile(inputPath).
  2. If operation == "encode":
       a. mimeType = file.mimeType (or FileHandler::guessMimeType).
       b. emoji = encodeBinary(mimeType, file.content).

                      (0 when emoji is empty) }.

       d. bytes = list[0] (EByteArray).
       e. Write bytes to inputPath via FileHandler::writeFile.
       f. result = { decoded_size: bytes.length, mime_type: mime }.
  4. Otherwise, return { error: "unknown operation", can_process: false }.
  5. Return result as a serialized EMap (String).
Related Features: compression, compressionMethod, emojiMap, reverseMap,
                  recipeType
Related Classes: CompressionMethod, FileData, FileHandler
Input:
  inputPath  (String) - path to the source file.
  outputPath (String) - path to the destination file.
  operation  (String) - either "encode" or "decode" (case-sensitive).
Output: String (EMap serialized) - file processing summary with keys
        original_bytes, encoded_length, mime_type, actual_ratio (encode)
        or decoded_size, mime_type (decode), or an error entry when the
        operation name is not recognized.
Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has run. For decode, outputPath
               contains an emoji string produced by this codec. The
               process has permission to read the input and write to
               the output.
Post-condition: After encode, outputPath holds an emoji string and the
               result map reports original_bytes and encoded_length.
               After decode, inputPath holds the recovered bytes and
               the result map reports decoded_size and mime_type.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: FreddyRodgers_emojichef

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system encodes text and binary files into emoji strings and decodes them back to their original data. It treats emoji characters as symbols in a configurable base alphabet, allowing ordinary bytes to be represented as compact emoji sequences. The system also supports optional compression, optional integrity hashing, file MIME preservation, and simple file-oriented encode/decode workflows.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Recipe selection controls the emoji alphabet size. The supported recipe names are `quick`, `light`, `classic`, and `gourmet`, with increasing capacities of 64, 128, 256, and 1024 symbols. The classic recipe represents 8 bits per emoji. Unknown recipes should fall back to classic behavior.

Text encoding should use UTF-8 bytes, optionally compress the byte stream, split the resulting bits into recipe-sized chunks, and map each chunk to an emoji symbol. Decoding should reverse this process and reject null input or symbols that are not part of the active emoji alphabet. Empty text should round-trip as an empty emoji string.

Compression mode `zlib` should use standard zlib-compatible compression and decompression. Compression mode `none` should leave bytes unchanged. Verification mode `sha256` should produce a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest with zero padding; verification mode `none` should produce an empty digest.

Binary data should be wrapped in a JSON-compatible structure before emoji encoding. The binary content is stored as Base64 text, and MIME type and original byte size must be preserved. The serialized field names are `content`, `mime_type`, and `size`. Decoding binary emoji data should restore the byte array and MIME type.

Encoding statistics should report `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `actual_ratio`, `theoretical_ratio`, and `bits_per_emoji`. File encoding results should include `original_bytes`, `encoded_length`, `mime_type`, and `actual_ratio`; file decoding results should include `decoded_size` and `mime_type`. File information results should include size, MIME type, whether the file can be processed, and a suggested recipe, or an error with `can_process` set to false.

Recipe suggestion is based on file size: small files below 1 KB use `quick`, files below 10 KB use `light`, files below 100 KB use `classic`, and larger files use `gourmet`.

File handling should read raw bytes, infer MIME type from the file name when possible, fall back to `application/octet-stream` when unknown, and write bytes while creating missing parent directories.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no helper class required outside the UML model.
```

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into an emoji string using the
   *          current recipe, optional compression, and the configured
   *          emoji alphabet.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
   *   2. Convert data to a UTF-8 byte array.
   *   3. Call processData(bytes) to apply optional compression.
   *   4. Convert the processed byte stream into a bit stream.
   *   5. Split the bit stream into chunks of bitsPerChunk bits each
   *      (zero-pad the final chunk if shorter).
   *   6. For each chunk, compute its integer value and look up the
   *      corresponding emoji symbol in emojiMap (values >= baseSize are
   *      impossible by construction of the chunk size).
   *   7. Concatenate the symbols and return the resulting emoji string.
   * Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, recipeType,
   *                   compression, compressionMethod, mask
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input: data (String) - the text to encode as UTF-8. May be empty.
   * Output: String - an emoji sequence representing the encoded data. Empty
   *         string when input is empty.
   * Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
   *                the recipe parameters are ready. The compression setting
   *                is one of the CompressionMethod constants.
   * Post-condition: decode(encode(data)) returns the original text for any
   *                 non-null UTF-8 string under the same configuration.

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text it
   *          represents, reversing the text encoding pipeline (unprocess,
   *          uncompress, UTF-8 decode).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If emojiData is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
   *   2. If emojiData is empty, return an empty string (round-trip case).
   *   3. Map each emoji symbol back to its chunk value via reverseMap;
   *      reject any symbol not present in reverseMap by throwing
   *      IllegalArgumentException.
   *   4. Concatenate the chunk bits into a single bit stream.
   *   5. Call unprocessData(bitStream) to reverse the optional compression
   *      step.
   *   6. Convert the resulting byte array to a UTF-8 String and return it.
   * Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, reverseMap, recipeType,
   *                   compression, compressionMethod, mask
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input: emojiData (String) - a non-null sequence of emoji symbols, each
   *        belonging to the currently configured alphabet. May be empty.
   * Output: String - the decoded UTF-8 text. Empty when input is empty.
   * Pre-condition: initializeIngredients() has been invoked so emojiMap and
   *                reverseMap are populated. compression is one of the values
   *                defined in CompressionMethod.
   * Post-condition: For non-empty input, all symbols are recognized; output is
   *                 valid UTF-8 and is the exact original text that would be

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Computes encoding statistics comparing an original text string
   *          and its emoji-encoded counterpart.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Compute original_bytes = UTF-8 byte length of `original`.
   *   2. Compute encoded_length = character count of `encoded` (each emoji
   *      symbol counts as one).
   *   3. bits_per_emoji = bitsPerChunk.
   *   4. theoretical_ratio = encoded_length * bits_per_emoji / original_bytes
   *      (or 0 when original_bytes is 0, to avoid division by zero).
   *   5. actual_ratio = original_bytes / encoded_length (or 0 when
   *      encoded_length is 0).
   *   6. Build an EMap with entries: original_bytes, encoded_length,
   *      actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji. Return it.
   * Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, recipeType
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input:
   *   original (String) - the source UTF-8 text, may be empty.
   *   encoded  (String) - the emoji-encoded text, may be empty.
   * Output: EMap - map with keys original_bytes, encoded_length,
   *         actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji.
   * Pre-condition: Both arguments are non-null. `encoded` is assumed to be
   *                the result of encode(original) under the current recipe.
   * Post-condition: The returned map is internally consistent:
   *                 theoretical_ratio uses bitsPerChunk derived from the recipe,
   *                 and ratios are zero when the relevant divisor is zero.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->

   * Summary: Computes encoding statistics comparing an original text string
   *          and its emoji-encoded counterpart.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Compute original_bytes = UTF-8 byte length of `original`.
   *   2. Compute encoded_length = character count of `encoded` (each emoji

   *   5. actual_ratio = original_bytes / encoded_length (or 0 when
   *      encoded_length is 0).

   *      actual_ratio, theoretical_ratio, bits_per_emoji. Return it.

  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    byte[] bytes = data.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    byte[] processed = processData(bytes);
    StringBuilder bits = new StringBuilder();
    for (byte b : processed)
    {
      for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--)
      {
        bits.append(((b >> i) & 1));
      }
    }
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    int bitsPerChunk = getBitsPerChunk();
    Map<Integer, String> emojiMap = getEmojiMap();
    int totalBits = bits.length();
    for (int i = 0; i < totalBits; i += bitsPerChunk)
    {
      int value = 0;
      for (int j = 0; j < bitsPerChunk; j++)
      {
        value <<= 1;
        if (i + j < totalBits)
        {
          value |= (bits.charAt(i + j) - '0');
        }
      }
      result.append(emojiMap.get(value));
    }
    return result.toString();
  }

  public String decode(final String emojiData)
  {
    if (emojiData == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("emojiData must not be null");
    }
    if (emojiData.isEmpty())
    {
      return "";
    }
    Map<String, Integer> reverseMap = getReverseMap();
    StringBuilder bits = new StringBuilder();
    int bitsPerChunk = getBitsPerChunk();
    int totalChars = emojiData.length();
    int charIndex = 0;
    while (charIndex < totalChars)
    {
      // Each emoji may be a surrogate pair or a single BMP character.
      int cp = emojiData.codePointAt(charIndex);
      int charCount = Character.charCount(cp);
      String symbol = emojiData.substring(charIndex, charIndex + charCount);
      charIndex += charCount;
      Integer value = reverseMap.get(symbol);
      if (value == null)
      {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown emoji symbol: " + symbol);
      }
      String chunkBits = Integer.toBinaryString(value);
      while (chunkBits.length() < bitsPerChunk)
      {
        chunkBits = "0" + chunkBits;
      }
      bits.append(chunkBits);
    }
    // Convert the bit stream to a byte array.
    int bitLen = bits.length();
    // The encoder zero-pads the final chunk to bitsPerChunk bits, so the bit
    // stream length is a multiple of bitsPerChunk. We may have trailing
    // padding bits that need to be stripped when converting back to bytes
    // (they represent zero bytes). The simplest approach is to use the
    // original_bytes tracking; however, here we simply pack 8 bits per byte
    // and rely on the upper bits being zero from the pad bits.
    int byteLen = bitLen / 8;
    byte[] bytes = new byte[byteLen];
    for (int i = 0; i < byteLen; i++)
    {
      int b = 0;
      for (int j = 0; j < 8; j++)
      {
        b = (b << 1) | (bits.charAt(i * 8 + j) - '0');
      }
      bytes[i] = (byte) b;
    }
    byte[] original = unprocessData(bytes);
    return new String(original, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  }

  public Map<String, Double> getStats(final String original, final String encoded)
  {
    int originalBytes = original.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length;
    int encodedLength = encoded.length();
    double bitsPerEmoji = getBitsPerChunk();
    double theoreticalRatio = (originalBytes == 0) ? 0.0 : ((double) (encodedLength * getBitsPerChunk())) / originalBytes;
    double actualRatio = (encodedLength == 0) ? 0.0 : ((double) originalBytes) / encodedLength;
    Map<String, Double> stats = new LinkedHashMap<String, Double>();
    stats.put("original_bytes", (double) originalBytes);
    stats.put("encoded_length", (double) encodedLength);
    stats.put("actual_ratio", actualRatio);
    stats.put("theoretical_ratio", theoreticalRatio);
    stats.put("bits_per_emoji", bitsPerEmoji);
    return stats;
  }

  public String encodeBinary(final String mimeType, final byte[] data)
  {
    PreparedData prepared = prepareBinaryData(mimeType, data);
    Map<String, Object> map = prepared.toMap();
    StringBuilder serialized = new StringBuilder();
    serialized.append("{");
    boolean first = true;
    for (Map.Entry<String, Object> entry : map.entrySet())
    {
      if (!first)
      {
        serialized.append(",");
      }
      first = false;
      serialized.append("\"").append(entry.getKey()).append("\":");
      Object value = entry.getValue();
      if (value == null)
      {
        serialized.append("null");
      }
      else if (value instanceof Number)
      {
        serialized.append(value.toString());
      }
      else
      {
        serialized.append("\"").append(value.toString()).append("\"");
      }
    }
    serialized.append("}");
    return encode(serialized.toString());
  }

  public Map<String, Object> processFile(final String inputPath, final String outputPath, final String operation)
  {
    Map<String, Object> result = new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    FileHandler handler = getFileHandler();
    if ("encode".equals(operation))
    {
      FileData file = handler.readFile(inputPath);
      String mimeType = file.getMimeType();
      if (mimeType == null)
      {
        mimeType = "application/octet-stream";
      }
      byte[] content = file.getContent();
      String emoji = encodeBinary(mimeType, content);
      handler.writeFile(outputPath, emoji.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
      int originalBytes = content.length;
      int encodedLength = emoji.length();
      double actualRatio = (encodedLength == 0) ? 0.0 : ((double) originalBytes) / encodedLength;
      result.put("original_bytes", originalBytes);
      result.put("encoded_length", encodedLength);
      result.put("mime_type", mimeType);
      result.put("actual_ratio", actualRatio);
    }
    else if ("decode".equals(operation))
    {
      FileData emojiFile = handler.readFile(outputPath);
      String emoji = new String(emojiFile.getContent(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
      EList<Object> list = decodeBinary(emoji);
      String mime = (String) list.get(1);
      byte[] bytes = (byte[]) list.get(0);
      handler.writeFile(inputPath, bytes);
      result.put("decoded_size", bytes.length);
      result.put("mime_type", mime);
    }
    else
    {
      result.put("error", "unknown operation");
      result.put("can_process", false);
    }
    return result;
  }

  public byte[] processData(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    CompressionMethod method = getCompressionMethod();
    String none = (method == null) ? null : method.getNone();
    if (getCompression() == null || getCompression().equals(none))
    {
      return data;
    }
    String zlib = (method == null) ? null : method.getZlib();
    if (getCompression().equals(zlib))
    {
      Deflater deflater = new Deflater();
      deflater.setInput(data);
      deflater.finish();
      ByteArrayOutputStream baos = new ByteArrayOutputStream(data.length);
      byte[] buf = new byte[1024];
      try
      {
        while (!deflater.finished())
        {
          int count = deflater.deflate(buf);
          baos.write(buf, 0, count);
        }
      }
      finally
      {
        deflater.end();
      }
      return baos.toByteArray();
    }
    return data;
  }

  public byte[] unprocessData(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    CompressionMethod method = getCompressionMethod();
    String none = (method == null) ? null : method.getNone();
    if (getCompression() == null || getCompression().equals(none))
    {
      return data;
    }
    String zlib = (method == null) ? null : method.getZlib();
    if (getCompression().equals(zlib))
    {
      Inflater inflater = new Inflater();
      inflater.setInput(data);
      ByteArrayOutputStream baos = new ByteArrayOutputStream(data.length * 2);
      byte[] buf = new byte[1024];
      try
      {
        while (!inflater.finished())
        {
          int count = inflater.inflate(buf);
          if (count == 0)
          {
            break;
          }
          baos.write(buf, 0, count);
        }
      }
      catch (java.util.zip.DataFormatException ex)
      {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Failed to decompress data", ex);
      }
      finally
      {
        inflater.end();
      }
      return baos.toByteArray();
    }
    return data;
  }

  public String calculateHash(final byte[] data)
  {
    if (data == null)
    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    VerificationMethod method = getVerificationMethod();
    String none = (method == null) ? null : method.getNone();
    if (getVerification() != null && getVerification().equals(none))
    {
      return "";
    }
    try
    {
      MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
      byte[] hash = digest.digest(data);
      StringBuilder hex = new StringBuilder(64);
      for (byte b : hash)
      {
        String h = Integer.toHexString(b & 0xFF);
        if (h.length() < 2)
        {
          hex.append('0');
        }
        hex.append(h);
      }
      return hex.toString();
    }
    catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException ex)
    {
      throw new IllegalStateException("SHA-256 algorithm not available", ex);
    }
  }

  private Map<String, Object> parseJsonLike(final String wrapper)
  {
    Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<String, Object>();
    String trimmed = wrapper.trim();
    if (trimmed.startsWith("{") && trimmed.endsWith("}"))
    {
      trimmed = trimmed.substring(1, trimmed.length() - 1).trim();
    }
    if (trimmed.isEmpty())
    {
      return map;
    }
    int i = 0;
    int len = trimmed.length();
    while (i < len)
    {
      // skip whitespace
      while (i < len && Character.isWhitespace(trimmed.charAt(i)))
      {
        i++;
      }
      if (i >= len)
      {
        break;
      }
      // read key (quoted)
      if (trimmed.charAt(i) != '"')
      {
        break;
      }
      i++;
      int keyStart = i;
      while (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) != '"')
      {
        i++;
      }
      String key = trimmed.substring(keyStart, i);
      i++; // skip closing quote
      // skip whitespace and ':'
      while (i < len && Character.isWhitespace(trimmed.charAt(i)))
      {
        i++;
      }
      if (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) == ':')
      {
        i++;
      }
      while (i < len && Character.isWhitespace(trimmed.charAt(i)))
      {
        i++;
      }
      // read value (quoted string or number)
      Object value;
      if (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) == '"')
      {
        i++;
        int valStart = i;
        while (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) != '"')
        {
          i++;
        }
        value = trimmed.substring(valStart, i);
        i++; // skip closing quote
      }
      else
      {
        int valStart = i;
        while (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) != ',')
        {
          i++;
        }
        String token = trimmed.substring(valStart, i).trim();
        if ("null".equals(token))
        {
          value = null;
        }
        else
        {
          try
          {
            value = Integer.parseInt(token);
          }
          catch (NumberFormatException nfe)
          {
            try
            {
              value = Double.parseDouble(token);
            }
            catch (NumberFormatException nfe2)
            {
              value = token;
            }
          }
        }
      }
      map.put(key, value);
      // skip ',' if present
      while (i < len && Character.isWhitespace(trimmed.charAt(i)))
      {
        i++;
      }
      if (i < len && trimmed.charAt(i) == ',')
      {
        i++;
      }
    }
    return map;
  }

  public String suggestRecipe(final int size)
  {
    if (size < 1024)
    {
      return "quick";
    }
    else if (size < 10240)
    {
      return "light";
    }
    else if (size < 102400)
    {
      return "classic";
    }
    else
    {
      return "gourmet";
    }
  }

   * Summary: Encodes a UTF-8 text string into an emoji string using the
   *          current recipe, optional compression, and the configured
   *          emoji alphabet.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If data is null, throw an IllegalArgumentException.
   *   2. Convert data to a UTF-8 byte array.
   *   3. Call processData(bytes) to apply optional compression.
   *   4. Convert the processed byte stream into a bit stream.
   *   5. Split the bit stream into chunks of bitsPerChunk bits each
   *      (zero-pad the final chunk if shorter).
   *   6. For each chunk, compute its integer value and look up the
   *      corresponding emoji symbol in emojiMap (values >= baseSize are
   *      impossible by construction of the chunk size).
   *   7. Concatenate the symbols and return the resulting emoji string.
   * Related Features: baseSize, bitsPerChunk, emojiMap, recipeType,
   *                   compression, compressionMethod, mask
   * Related Classes: CompressionMethod
   * Input: data (String) - the text to encode as UTF-8. May be empty.
   * Output: String - an emoji sequence representing the encoded data. Empty

  public String encode(final String data)
  {

    {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("data must not be null");
    }
    byte[] bytes = data.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    byte[] processed = processData(bytes);
    StringBuilder bits = new StringBuilder(processed.length * 8);
    for (byte b : processed)
    {
      for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--)
      {
        bits.append((b >> i) & 1);
      }
    }
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    int chunkBits = getBitsPerChunk();
    Map<Integer, String> map = getEmojiMap();

    for (int i = 0; i < totalBits; i += chunkBits)

      int value = 0;

      {
        value <<= 1;

   * Summary: Decodes an emoji string back into the original UTF-8 text it
